Yes, I read the changelog before upgrading. The problem is that the changelog doesn't say what changed.

I found the cause today. It is PR #812 ("refactor spectral frame handling", merged Oct 22). In LineList.__init__ the default went from wave_frame='air' to wave_frame='vacuum'. So rest wavelengths are now vacuum by default, while my spectra are calibrated in air from arc lamps. The vacuum/air ratio at 6563 Å is about 1.00028, which is exactly the offset I reported (about 83 km/s), in the same direction for every object.

So this is a changed default in the library, not a problem with my calibration or my config. The same spectra and the same config file give different redshifts in 2.4.3 and 2.5.0.

About "works for me": that is not a test. If your data is already in vacuum wavelengths, or it is radio, of course you see no difference. Anyone with air-calibrated optical data who doesn't set wave_frame explicitly will get shifted redshifts. m_okonkwo also reported an offset on long-slit data above, so it is probably not only me.

CHANGES.md for 2.5.0 says only "Refactor LineList and spectral frame handling (#812)". Nobody can guess from the word "refactor" that a default changed, and there is no deprecation warning. This thread was marked solved after I was told it was almost certainly my own calibration, so I spent two days re-reducing arc lamps for 40 spectra. The calibration was fine the whole time.

Workaround for anyone who finds this thread: set the frame explicitly when you build the line list.

LineList(..., wave_frame='air')

That is what fixed it for me.

To the maintainers, three requests:

1. Please reopen this thread. It is not solved, and it was not a user error.
2. Add a line to CHANGES.md for 2.5.0 saying that the default wave_frame changed from 'air' to 'vacuum'.
3. Emit a warning when wave_frame is not set, at least for a release or two, so people notice before they publish shifted redshifts.

I can send a minimal example if that helps.
